name: Arusha National Park
summary: A small, varied park beside Arusha with Mount Meru, the Momella lakes, giraffes and colobus monkeys, ideal for a day trip.
description:
Arusha National Park lies about 25 kilometres from Arusha and packs a surprising amount into a small area: the forested slopes of Mount Meru, the Ngurdoto Crater, and the Momella lakes, where flamingos and other water birds gather.
It is one of the few northern parks where you can get out of the vehicle on a guided walking safari with an armed ranger, and it is a quiet place for photography. Giraffes, buffalo, warthogs, zebras and black-and-white colobus monkeys are the main sights. You will not find the big predators of the Serengeti here, which is part of its relaxed charm.
Because it is so close to the city, it works well as a day trip on arrival or departure day, or as a gentle start before Tarangire, the Serengeti and Ngorongoro.
getting_there: The park gate is about 45 minutes from Arusha, so a half-day or full-day visit works easily on arrival or departure day.
best_time: June to October and December to February, for the clearest views of Mount Meru
best_weather: Cooler than the lowlands, especially in the mornings

highlights.b: A chain of shallow lakes with flamingos and other water birds.
A forested crater with a small wildlife-filled floor.
Black-and-white colobus monkeys swing through the forest canopy.
Easy to see on the open grassland.
Dramatic views of the volcano from the park.

activities.a: Guided walking safari with a ranger
Canoe safari on the Momella lakes

tips.a: Bring a light jacket as the park sits high on the slopes of Mount Meru.
Early mornings give the clearest mountain views.
Walking safaris must be done with a ranger.
Combine with a visit to the coffee farms nearby.

name: Arusha
summary: The lively gateway city of the northern circuit, beneath Mount Meru and about an hour from Kilimanjaro Airport.
description:
Arusha sits at the foot of Mount Meru and is where most northern Tanzania safaris begin and end. Kilimanjaro International Airport is roughly an hour away by road, so many guests arrive, rest for a night and set off the next morning.
It is worth giving the city a little time. The Cultural Heritage Centre and the craft markets are good for gifts, the coffee farms and waterfalls on Meru's lower slopes make easy half-day outings, and Arusha National Park is only a short drive away.
The city lies at about 1,400 metres, so days are warm and evenings can be cool. Hotels range from simple guesthouses to comfortable lodges set in gardens, and we can arrange your airport transfers and first and last nights as part of any package.
getting_there: Kilimanjaro International Airport is roughly an hour from Arusha by road, and Arusha Airport has scheduled flights to the Serengeti, Zanzibar and other airstrips.
best_time: All year; June to October is the driest
high_season: July to October and December to January
best_weather: Warm days and cool evenings, with rain mostly from March to May

highlights.b: On clear mornings the mountain towers over the city.
A large gallery and shop with carvings, paintings and jewellery.
Busy local markets for spices, fabric and everyday life.
Easy half-day visits to estates on the slopes of Mount Meru.
The starting point for nearly every northern safari.

activities.a: Visit to the Cultural Heritage Centre
Day trip to Arusha National Park

tips.a: Spend a night before or after your safari to rest.
Carry small notes in Tanzanian shillings for markets.
Use hotel-arranged taxis at night.
Ask us about airport transfers and city stays.

name: Usambara Mountains
summary: Cool mountain villages, forests and viewpoints.
description:
The Usambara Mountains, in north-eastern Tanzania, are part of the Eastern Arc range and are known for their cool climate, terraced farms, forest reserves and wide views over the plains. The area is excellent for walking between villages, with local guides, and is rich in birdlife and endemic plants.
It suits travellers who want a quiet, cultural walking experience away from the main safari parks, and it is typically reached from Arusha or Tanga. Trails are mostly moderate and can be muddy in the rains, so good footwear is useful.
getting_there: Lushoto, the main base in the Western Usambaras, is around five to six hours by road from Arusha or Dar es Salaam.
best_weather: June to October (dry); the mountains are cool and can be misty

highlights.b: Pleasant temperatures and green hills a world away from the heat of the coast.
Day hikes between farms, forests and small communities.
Dramatic overlooks across the plains, such as Irente.
The mountains are part of the Eastern Arc, home to many species found nowhere else.
Few tourists, with local guides who know the trails.

activities.a: Visits to local markets and farms

tips.a: Bring a warm layer and rain jacket as it can be cool and misty.
Hire a local guide for trails.
June to October is the driest period.
Combine it with a safari for contrast.

name: Mount Meru
summary: A rewarding climb and a good Kilimanjaro warm-up.
description:
Mount Meru, at 4,566 metres, is the second-highest mountain in Tanzania and rises above Arusha National Park. The standard route, from Momella Gate, takes in forest, a crater rim and a long, narrow ridge, with a good chance of seeing buffalo, giraffe and monkeys on the lower slopes, which is why an armed ranger accompanies each group.
Meru is a challenging climb in its own right, usually done in three to four days, and it is also a well-regarded acclimatisation trek before Kilimanjaro. The views of Kilimanjaro at sunrise from the crater rim are a highlight.
getting_there: Momella Gate is around 45 minutes from Arusha by road, so you can start trekking on the same day you arrive.

highlights.b: Meru rises to 4,566 metres above Arusha National Park.
Giraffes, buffalo and monkeys are often seen on the lower slopes with an armed ranger.
The crater rim walk to Socialist Peak has spectacular views.
A popular acclimatisation hike before Kilimanjaro.
Fewer climbers than on Kilimanjaro.

activities.a: Three- to four-day Momella route trek
Wildlife walk through Arusha National Park

tips.a: An armed ranger accompanies every group.
The dry months from June to February are best.
Bring warm clothes and rain protection.
Combine it with a safari for a balanced trip.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
description:
Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest mountain in Africa, and the world's tallest free-standing mountain, rising to 5,895 metres at Uhuru Peak. You do not need technical climbing skills to reach the summit, but it is a serious high-altitude trek, and the biggest factor in success is giving your body enough time to acclimatise, which is why longer routes have better summit rates.
There are several routes, each with its own character: Marangu, with huts; Machame and Lemosho, with scenic camps and a gradual profile; Rongai, from the north, which is drier; Umbwe, steep and direct; and the Northern Circuit, the longest route and the best for acclimatisation. The mountain passes through rainforest, moorland, alpine desert and a summit zone of ice and rock, and the weather can change quickly.
The main climbing seasons are January to March and June to October. All climbs must be done with a registered guide, and we provide guides, porters and cooks. Training, good gear and a calm pace matter more than raw fitness.
getting_there: Kilimanjaro International Airport is about an hour from Moshi and the main park gates. Our team collects you from the airport and takes you to your hotel.
best_time: January to March and June to October

highlights.b: At 5,895 metres, the roof of Africa and the highest free-standing mountain in the world.
Rainforest, moorland, alpine desert and glaciers in a single trek.
Marangu, Machame, Lemosho, Rongai, Umbwe and the Northern Circuit.
Most climbers reach the top at dawn after a midnight start.
Guides, cooks and porters carry equipment and prepare meals.

activities.a: Day hike to Marangu Gate or the Materuni waterfalls
Safari or Zanzibar extension after the climb

tips.a: Longer routes give your body more time to adjust and a better chance of reaching the summit.
Pack warm layers, a good sleeping bag and well-worn boots.
Walk slowly and drink plenty of water.
Train with long hikes and stairs before you come.

name: Zanzibar
summary: Stone Town, spice farms and Indian Ocean beaches.
description:
Zanzibar is a tropical island off the Tanzanian coast with white-sand beaches, clear water and a long Swahili and Omani history. Stone Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is a maze of narrow lanes, carved doors, markets and old merchant houses, and it is worth at least a half day on foot with a guide.
Outside Stone Town, you can visit spice farms, swim with dolphins, snorkel on the coral reefs or simply relax on the beach. The north and east coasts have different characters: the north coast, around Nungwi and Kendwa, has deeper water for swimming at all tides, while the east coast has big tidal changes, which affect swimming and water sports. Zanzibar is a natural end to a safari, and the main seasons are the dry months from June to October and January to February.
getting_there: Fly from Arusha, Kilimanjaro or Dar es Salaam to Zanzibar, or take a ferry from Dar es Salaam, which takes about two hours.
best_time: June to October and January to February (drier, sunnier months)
high_season: July to August and December to January

highlights.b: A historic UNESCO World Heritage old town of narrow lanes, carved doors and Swahili markets.
Tours that let you taste and smell cloves, vanilla, cinnamon and nutmeg.
From Nungwi and Kendwa in the north to Paje and Jambiani on the east coast.
Home to the rare red colobus monkey.
Clear water around Mnemba Atoll and Prison Island.

activities.a: Visit to Jozani Forest to see red colobus monkeys

tips.a: Dress modestly in Stone Town and away from the beach.
East-coast beaches change dramatically with the tides.
The long rains in April and May are the quietest period.
Add three or four nights after a safari to relax.

name: Ruaha National Park
summary: Rugged country and big lion prides.
description:
Ruaha National Park is the largest national park in Tanzania, a wild and rugged landscape of baobab-studded hills, open bush and the seasonal Great Ruaha River. It is known for large prides of lion, strong numbers of elephant and buffalo, and a mix of species seen less often further north, such as greater kudu and sable and roan antelope.
The best wildlife viewing is in the dry season, from roughly June to October, when game concentrates along the river. Ruaha is remote and usually reached by a light aircraft, with a small number of camps and very few vehicles, so it appeals to travellers who value space and solitude over a busy schedule.
getting_there: Most guests fly from Dar es Salaam or Arusha, which takes roughly an hour and a half to two hours. You can also drive from Iringa in around three hours.
best_time: June to October (animals gather along the river)

highlights.b: The lifeline of the park and the best place to see wildlife in the dry season.
Ruaha is known for large groups of lions and many other predators.
Large herds roam beneath old baobab trees.
Greater and lesser kudu, sable and roan antelope are seen here more often than in the north.
The park is large and remote and few other visitors are around.

activities.a: Fly camping in the bush (on request)

tips.a: Visit from June to October when animals gather at the river.
Choose a camp close to the river for the best game viewing.
Bring lightweight, neutral clothing.
Give yourself three nights to make the journey worthwhile.

name: Nyerere National Park
summary: Boats, walks and the wild south.
description:
Nyerere National Park, formerly the northern part of the Selous Game Reserve, is one of the largest protected areas in Africa and is centred on the Rufiji River and its network of lakes and channels. Unlike most Tanzanian parks it allows boat safaris and guided walking safaris, in addition to game drives, so you can see hippo, crocodile and elephants from the water and track wildlife on foot.
Wildlife includes elephant, buffalo, giraffe, lion, wild dog and a very large bird list. The park is remote, usually reached by short scheduled flight, and has few vehicles. It suits travellers who want a quieter safari and an alternative to the Northern Circuit, or a second trip. Some camps close in the wettest months, so dates should be checked when planning.
getting_there: The simplest way is a short scheduled or charter flight from Dar es Salaam of about 45 minutes. Drives from Dar es Salaam take six to seven hours.
best_weather: June to October (dry); some camps close in the wettest months

highlights.b: Boat safaris glide past hippos, crocodiles and drinking elephants.
Guided walks with an armed ranger let you see the smaller details of the bush.
The park has good chances of seeing this endangered predator.
Water views make the scenery very different from the northern parks.
Large wilderness with very few other vehicles.

activities.a: Boat safari on the Rufiji River

tips.a: June to October is the best season for game viewing.
Wear neutral colours as tsetse flies can be present.
Pack light for the small bush planes.
Roads may be difficult during the rainy season.

name: Mikumi National Park
summary: Easy-access savanna close to Dar es Salaam.
description:
Mikumi National Park is one of the most accessible safari parks in Tanzania, within a few hours' drive of Dar es Salaam and with scheduled flights from Zanzibar. Its open floodplain, the Mkata plain, is good for giraffe, zebra, buffalo, wildebeest, elephant and hippo, and lion are seen with some regularity.
Because of its location, Mikumi works well as a short safari from Dar es Salaam or Zanzibar and as a gentle introduction to the southern circuit. It is also easy to combine with the Udzungwa Mountains. It is quieter than the north, with fewer vehicles, although the main road runs along one edge of the park.
getting_there: Mikumi is about four hours by road from Dar es Salaam, or you can fly to a nearby airstrip, and it is a natural first stop on the southern circuit.

highlights.b: A wide, open plain where giraffes, zebra, buffalo and elephants are easy to spot.
A pool where you can get out to watch hippos from a safe viewing area.
The easiest national park to reach from the coast.
Resident prides and elephant herds, often seen from the main road through the park.
More than 400 species have been recorded.

activities.a: Day visit to the nearby Udzungwa Mountains for forest walks

tips.a: The main highway crosses the park, so watch for slow speed limits and wildlife on the road.
June to October is the driest and best time.
Combine it with Ruaha or Nyerere for a longer southern trip.
Bring insect repellent for evenings.

name: Oldoinyo Lengai & Lake Natron
summary: Oldoinyo Lengai volcano and the flamingo-lined Lake Natron.
description:
Oldoinyo Lengai, the Mountain of God in the Maasai language, is an active volcano in the north of the Rift Valley, and Lake Natron lies just below it. The lake is a shallow, very alkaline soda lake and one of the most important breeding grounds for lesser flamingos in East Africa, set in a stark, dramatic landscape of salt flats, escarpment and waterfalls.
The region is remote and hot, with limited facilities, and offers walking, cultural visits and waterfall hikes. The climb of Oldoinyo Lengai is a steep, demanding overnight ascent that begins around midnight to reach the crater rim before sunrise, so it is suitable only for fit walkers who are comfortable on loose volcanic ground. Conditions at the summit can change, so we plan this with local guides and confirm the route before you go.
getting_there: Lake Natron is a long day by 4x4 from Arusha, roughly four to five hours depending on the route and conditions, on mostly unpaved roads.
best_time: June to October (dry); flamingos usually breed from roughly July to October
best_weather: June to October (little to no rain)

highlights.b: The Maasai "Mountain of God" is an active volcano that erupts unusual carbonatite lava.
A hot, alkaline lake in the Rift Valley that is the main breeding ground for lesser flamingos in East Africa.
A shady gorge with a waterfall and pools, reached by a short walk.
Cracked salt flats, red rocks and almost no other visitors.
The area is home to Maasai communities who herd livestock across the plains.

activities.a: Night climb of Ol Doinyo Lengai (strenuous)
Walk to the Engare Sero waterfall and gorge
Flamingo watching along the lake shore

tips.a: The Lengai climb starts around midnight and is steep and loose, so good fitness is needed.
It is hot and dry, so carry plenty of water and sun protection.
Flamingo numbers vary through the year.
Allow at least two nights to make the trip worthwhile.

name: Lake Eyasi
summary: A cultural stop with Hadzabe and Datoga communities.
description:
Lake Eyasi is a shallow, seasonal soda lake in the Rift Valley south of the Serengeti, and it is best known as a cultural destination rather than a game park. The area is home to the Hadzabe, one of the last hunter-gatherer communities in Africa, and to Datoga pastoralists and blacksmiths.
Visits are usually arranged with local guides and include a morning hunting walk with Hadzabe hunters, or a visit to a Datoga homestead. These are best approached as respectful, small-group visits, with the community benefiting directly. The area is hot and dry, so an early start and sun protection matter, and the lake level changes a lot between seasons. Lake Eyasi sits naturally between Lake Manyara and Ngorongoro on a longer Northern Circuit itinerary.
getting_there: Lake Eyasi is about one and a half hours on dirt road from Karatu, which is itself roughly two and a half to three hours from Arusha, so most guests spend a night in the area.
best_weather: June to October (little to no rain)

highlights.b: One of the last hunter-gatherer communities in Africa, who share their way of life with respectful visitors.
Skilled blacksmiths and herders who make jewellery and tools by hand.
A shallow, seasonal soda lake with flamingos and other water birds.
Open woodland to explore on foot with a local guide.
Remote camps with very dark skies.

activities.a: Early-morning bush walk with Hadzabe hunters
Visit to a Datoga village and blacksmith
Walking along the shore and watching birds

tips.a: Visits take place at sunrise, so expect an early start.
Ask your guide before taking photographs and follow their advice.
Bring closed shoes and long trousers for bush walking.
Fees go directly to the communities you visit.

name: Lake Manyara National Park
summary: A compact park of forest, flamingos and tree-climbing lions.
description:
Lake Manyara National Park lies at the foot of the Rift Valley escarpment and packs a wide variety of habitats into a small area: groundwater forest, acacia woodland, open grassland and the shallow alkaline lake itself. It is a good park for large troops of baboons, blue monkeys, elephants, hippo, giraffe and an exceptional range of birds, including flamingos and pelicans when water levels suit them.
The park is known for tree-climbing lions, although sightings are never guaranteed. The lake changes with the rains, so what you see varies by season, and the park is often combined with Tarangire or Ngorongoro rather than visited on its own. It is a gentle, scenic day or half day that suits families and travellers who want variety rather than big herds.
getting_there: The park is about two hours from Arusha by road and lies on the way to Ngorongoro and the Serengeti, so it slots easily into most northern itineraries.
best_time: June to October for wildlife, and November to April for birds

highlights.b: Lions here are famous for resting in the branches, although it is never guaranteed.
Shady mahogany and fig trees full of baboons and blue monkeys greet you at the gate.
Flamingos and pelicans line the shore when water levels are right, with hippos in the pools.
The Rift Valley wall rises behind the park and gives dramatic views.
A treetop walkway lets you see the forest from above.

activities.a: Cultural tour and bicycle ride in nearby Mto wa Mbu village

tips.a: A half day is enough for most guests.
Water levels change through the year, which affects how many birds you will see on the lake.
Bring binoculars for the birds and the monkeys in the forest.
Combine it with Mto wa Mbu village for local food and crafts.

name: Tarangire National Park
summary: Elephants, baobabs and dry-season game viewing.
description:
Tarangire National Park is known for its big elephant herds and its ancient baobab trees, which dot a landscape of rolling hills, swamps and the permanent Tarangire River. It is one of the best parks in Tanzania for elephants and has a rich bird list, along with lion, leopard, giraffe, zebra, wildebeest and the occasional python seen in the trees.
The park is at its best in the dry season, from about June to October, when animals from the surrounding plains gather along the river and wildlife viewing is concentrated and easy. During the wet months the park turns green and quieter, with excellent birding but wildlife more spread out.
Tarangire is close to Arusha, about two to three hours by road, which makes it a popular first stop on the Northern Circuit and a practical choice for a one-day or two-day trip.
getting_there: Tarangire is about two to two and a half hours by road from Arusha on a good surface, which makes it a convenient first stop on a northern circuit.
best_time: June to October (animals gather along the river)

highlights.b: In the dry season large family groups gather along the Tarangire River, and the park is known for big tuskers.
Huge, ancient baobabs dot the hills and make striking photographs.
Zebra, wildebeest, buffalo and antelope crowd the river when water elsewhere dries up.
Hundreds of species are recorded, including the colourful yellow-collared lovebird and many raptors.
Fewer vehicles than the Serengeti or Ngorongoro, with long stretches of peaceful scenery.

activities.a: Bird watching, especially in the green season
Walking and night safaris in neighbouring conservation areas, arranged separately

tips.a: The dry months from June to October give the best game viewing.
Tsetse flies can be a nuisance in some areas, so wear neutral clothes and avoid dark blue and black.
Stay at least one night to see the park at dawn and dusk.
It combines well with Lake Manyara, Ngorongoro and the Serengeti.

name: Ngorongoro Crater
summary: A UNESCO-listed caldera packed with wildlife.
description:
The Ngorongoro Crater is the world's largest intact volcanic caldera, about 260 square kilometres across, with walls that rise some 600 metres above the floor. Because the crater is so enclosed, wildlife can be found in a small area: lion, hyena, buffalo, elephant, hippo, flamingos on the soda lake and, with luck, the endangered black rhino.
Most visits are a single early-morning descent with a picnic lunch on the crater floor, followed by a climb back to the rim in the afternoon. The rim sits at around 2,300 metres, so evenings are cool and mornings can be misty, and a warm layer is useful even in the dry season. The wider Ngorongoro Conservation Area is a multiple-use area where Maasai pastoralists live alongside wildlife, and it also includes Olduvai Gorge, a key site for the study of early humans.
The crater is busy in peak months, so an early start makes a real difference to the experience. It combines naturally with the Serengeti, Tarangire and Lake Manyara on the Northern Circuit.
getting_there: The crater rim is about three hours by road from Arusha through Mto wa Mbu and Karatu on tarmac, followed by a steep gravel track down to the floor in a 4x4 safari vehicle.
best_time: June to October (wildlife viewing is best)
best_weather: June to October (little to no rain)

highlights.b: One of the largest unbroken volcanic craters in the world, about 600 metres deep and 20 kilometres across.
The crater is one of the few places in Tanzania where this rare animal is seen with some regularity.
Lions, elephants, hippos, buffalo, zebra and wildebeest share a small, easy-to-cover floor.
A shallow soda lake that attracts flamingos at certain times of year.
Nearby, a famous site in the study of early human origins, with a small museum.

activities.a: Crater floor game drive (limited to about six hours)
Picnic lunch beside the Ngoitokitok springs
Visit to Olduvai Gorge and its museum
Cultural visit to a Maasai village on the highlands

tips.a: The rim sits at roughly 2,300 metres and mornings are cold, so bring a warm jacket.
Descend at first light to enjoy the floor before the other vehicles arrive.
Visitors may stay on the floor for a limited time each day, so plan your picnic stop in advance.
Keep a camera with a zoom lens ready for the rhinos, which are often far away.

name: Serengeti National Park
summary: Endless plains, big cats and the Great Migration.
description:
The Serengeti is Tanzania's best-known park, a vast ecosystem of open grassland, kopjes (granite outcrops) and river woodland that stretches north towards Kenya's Maasai Mara. It is home to lion, leopard, cheetah, elephant, giraffe, hippo and enormous herds of plains game, and it is one of the few places where you can reliably find all of the big cats in a single trip.
The park is best known for the wildebeest migration, in which well over a million wildebeest, along with zebra and gazelle, follow the rains in a rough circle through the ecosystem. Calving takes place on the southern plains around Ndutu from roughly December to March. The herds move through the central and western Serengeti in the middle of the year, and the dramatic Mara River crossings in the north usually happen between about July and October. Exact timing changes from year to year, so a good itinerary stays flexible.
Good to know: the Serengeti is large, so most visitors spend two to three nights to see more than one area. Game drives start early and finish late, and many lodges and camps are small and seasonal. Wildlife is excellent all year, and the best choice of area depends on the month you travel.
getting_there: Most guests drive from Arusha through Lake Manyara or Tarangire and Ngorongoro, which takes a full day to the central Serengeti, or fly from Arusha, Manyara or Zanzibar to an airstrip such as Seronera in about an hour and a half.
best_time: January to February and June to October (different areas are best at different times)
high_season: July to March (the Seronera area is busy)
best_weather: June to October (little to no rain)

highlights.b: Around 1.5 million wildebeest, with zebra and gazelle, follow the rains in a great loop through the Serengeti and into Kenya's Maasai Mara.
Lions, leopards and cheetahs are seen regularly, particularly around the Seronera valley and the open southern plains.
Year-round water draws wildlife, making it a dependable area for game drives in any month.
Granite outcrops rise from the plains and are favourite lookouts for lions and cheetahs.
The wide skies and golden grass are some of the best landscapes in Africa for photography.

activities.a: Bush picnic lunches on the plains
Watching river crossings in the north (usually July to October)

tips.a: The herds move with the rain, so tell us your dates and we will place you in the right part of the park.
Start early: animals are most active at first light and in the late afternoon.
Bring binoculars, a hat and a light scarf for the dust.
Park fees and the safari vehicle are included in our packages.
